{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABXsao5A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhBQrMo", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 29, "title": "Add bounded BufferNode vec4/mat4 round-trip support", "body": "## Problem

The Draft v2.0 reference exporter/loader now support bounded `UniformArrayNode` data (#25) and shared `UniformNode` group links (#27), but ordinary `BufferNode` instances are still unsupported. `BufferNode` represents explicitly typed/count-limited uniform-buffer arrays (including `vec4` and `mat4`) and is not interchangeable with `UniformArrayNode`, whose native padding and upload behavior differ.

Extend the **existing** plugins with a small, data-only `BufferNode` subset where the native Three.js meaning can be preserved. Do not treat arbitrary buffers, render/compute resources, or geometry attributes as part of this issue.

## Expected outcome

1. **Audit the actual Three.js r186 implementation** (recheck current stable during implementation): `BufferNode`, `UniformNode`/`InputNode`, native `ArrayElementNode`, default `element()` behavior, `getSerializeChildren()`, `serialize()/deserialize()`, group/update state, and GLSL/WGSL uniform-buffer layout and binding behavior. Record the constructor versus mutable/generated state, correct buffer element count, type inference, and accepted native value representation(s).
2. Implement **paired default exporter serialization and loader resolution** for a *verified* bounded subset:
   - Target `bufferType = 'vec4'` and `bufferType = 'mat4'` with explicit, positive `bufferCount`, matching finite numeric data, valid native shape/ordering, and conservative size limits grounded in tests.
   - Save a portable **snapshot** of source values, effective type and element count in JSON. Recreate native Three.js `BufferNode` objects; never serialize a GPU buffer, runtime cache, renderer object, raw shader source, or executable callback.
   - Preserve ordinary element access through existing `ArrayElementNode` parent/index links, graph sharing, repeated material entrypoints, and compatible existing `IndexNode` forms. Ensure the linked `BufferNode` is actually reconstructed rather than silently coerced to `UniformArrayNode`.
   - Use native Three.js generation, layout and buffer management. Reuse the current graph writer/loader, explicit adapters and link validation; avoid duplicating shader calculations or creating a generic buffer transport framework.
   - Preserve only group/lifecycle/value states for which the **existing** glTF material graph can retain Three.js semantics. Default `objectGroup` is the baseline; expand to other exact groups only if the native renderer and cross-material sharing tests establish correctness.
3. If native `vec4` or `mat4` shapes, GLTF round trips, or GLSL/WGSL backend behavior cannot be faithfully preserved, **defer that exact case with the source-level reason and a proposed paired adapter path**. Do not claim both variants supported based only on constructor fields or JSON equality.
4. Reject unsupported or ambiguous variants explicitly: arbitrary `bufferType`/layouts, inconsistent `bufferCount` and lengths, invalid/NaN/infinite data, renderer-owned GPU/storage/compute buffers, app callbacks, unsupported update ranges/custom groups, unknown own state or child links, and subclasses masquerading as built-in `BufferNode`. If typed array inputs are supported, specify precisely which kinds and snapshot semantics; otherwise defer them explicitly. Native partial-upload/update-range semantics must not be silently lost.
5. Validate import args, bounds, node-reference links and types *before* publishing any material graph. On any malformed or unsupported graph (including unreachable nodes or invalid element/index links), retain the **entire ordinary glTF material and supported other glTF extensions** as Draft v2.0 requires. Never partially apply entrypoints.
6. Keep Draft v2.0, `materialType` restoration, ordinary glTF material-property coexistence and the v1.0 removal unchanged. No Three.js core changes unless source evidence establishes that existing plugin hooks are genuinely insufficient. No file-provided JavaScript/GLSL/WGSL.

## Context and reproduction

- [Draft v2.0](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/README.md)
- [Default node coverage / deferred BufferNode](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md)
- [Uniform-array audit (#25)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/uniform-array-support.md)
- [Uniform-group audit (#27)](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/uniform-group-support.md)
- [Exporter serializer](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/defaultNodeSerializer.ts)
- [Loader resolver](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/defaultNodeResolver.ts)
- [Real integration suites](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/demo/test)
- [Three.js r186 BufferNode source](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/BufferNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 ArrayElementNode source](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/utils/ArrayElementNode.js)

Representative use case: `buffer(flatMatrixValues, 'mat4', count).element(index)` or the analogous `vec4` data source in a supported mesh NodeMaterial graph. Currently the default exporter does not support the parent `BufferNode` even when its `ArrayElementNode` link shape is otherwise supported.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Record the installed/current Three.js source audit, exact supported data representations, type/count/byte limits, input/index restrictions, renderer/back-end behavior, and explicit deferrals with reasons.
- [ ] Implement paired, minimal `BufferNode` defaults for each **verified** `vec4`/`mat4` variant in the existing plugin structure. Correctly preserve native type/count/value and existing element links without adding code execution or new extension fields.
- [ ] Add real GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader → GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader tests (JSON glTF and relevant GLB cases) for supported types and sizes, shared buffer/index references, material entrypoints, ordinary material properties and fallback. Compare native buffer contents/ordering and shader flow, not just graph JSON.
- [ ] Compare native GLSL/WGSL setup/analyze/generate behavior before and after import where the r186 renderer supports the tested stage; check representative `vec4` and matrix indexing in meaningful vertex/fragment contexts. Validate legitimate native data updates and document what cannot be checked without a live renderer.
- [ ] Add negative exporter/import tests for type/count/shape errors, unexpected links/state, unsupported layouts, callback/update-range/group variants, invalid/out-of-range constant indices, cycles, bad references and malformed unreachable definitions. Verify atomic fallback to the full ordinary glTF material.
- [ ] Update the coverage matrix and affected loader/exporter READMEs with the **precise** tested subset and deferred cases; keep Draft v2.0 and existing shared nodes unchanged.
- [ ] Run and report the actual full demo test suite, loader/exporter builds, demo typecheck/build, and `git diff --check`, including any warnings, failures and skips. Do not invent a repository-wide test script.

## Optional validation

WebGL/WebGPU visual smoke tests of indexed `vec4` and `mat4` values and runtime updates. State clearly if not run: Node-side GLSL/WGSL generation does not prove GPU compilation, upload behavior, or rendered pixels.

## Required post-merge verification

None. **No npm publication or package version bump in this issue**; the maintainer performs releases and `npm publish` manually in a separate step.
